title: Where agent work starts
ask: How does a person hand work to an agent?
why: The current page (a task box, agent and ticket drop-downs, a raw transcript) is the form-plus-transcript pattern every reference repo regretted. This choice shapes every agent screen.
learn: Paperclip issue threads and wakeups; lc-wms advance per lane and the /do dispatcher; control-center's audit of four entry points (research 12)
rec_reason: Work stays attached to its ticket, the stage already knows the next role, and one click replaces three fields. The assistant remains for plain-language requests and routes them onto tickets instead of being a separate place.

options.label: Ticket thread, Next step and Crew
options.desc: Runs live on the ticket thread. Next step picks the role from the stage; @role mentions hand work over; a Crew page shows who is doing what; the assistant routes plain requests into plan cards.
pros: One place per piece of work
No drop-downs: the stage picks the role
Chat and runs are the same thread
cons: Work without a ticket goes through the assistant
options.pick_if: most agent work belongs to a ticket.

options.label: Keep a chat-first agents page
options.desc: Improve today's page: one composer, the agent guessed from the message, a nicer transcript.
cons: Results still have to be copied to the ticket
options.pick_if: you mostly run one-off tasks outside tickets.

options.label: Board buttons only
options.desc: One advance button per lane on the board, no chat with agents.
cons: No way to steer or talk to a running agent
options.pick_if: agents should run unattended end to end.

title: The model engine for any OpenAI-compatible model
ask: How do agents run on OpenRouter, LM Studio or DeepSeek models, next to Claude Code and Cursor?
why: CLI agents bring their own loop and tools; a plain model does not. Something has to supply the loop, the tools, the approvals and the context management.
learn: deepseek-harness agent loop, tools, session log, compaction (research 12)
rec_reason: A small loop of our own fits the plugin kernel, reuses the providers, approval queue and verbs we already have, and copies deepseek-harness's proven mechanisms without its ceremony. Running deepseek-harness as a separate CLI is a cheaper fallback if the loop slips.

options.label: Our own small loop (Helmlock loop)
options.desc: A runtime plugin: turn and step loop over the providers plugin, tools (read, grep, glob, edit with read-before-edit, shell with ask, hl verbs, todo, skill, ask_user, finish), session event log, compaction ladder, the same approval queue.
pros: One approval queue and one event vocabulary for both engines
Fits the kernel and our verbs
cons: The biggest piece of new code
Small local models may be weak at tool use
options.pick_if: you want any model to work tickets like a CLI agent does.

options.label: Run deepseek-harness as another CLI engine
options.desc: Treat the dsh CLI like Claude Code: spawn it, parse its stream, map its approvals.
cons: Another tool to install and keep up to date
Its own config, skills and approvals beside ours

options.label: Models only for the assistant
options.desc: Keep models for chat and routing; code work runs only on CLI agents.
cons: OpenRouter and local models never do ticket work
options.pick_if: you will always have a Claude or Cursor subscription.

title: How a run's result reaches the ticket
ask: How does the ticket learn what a run did?
why: lc-wms scraped STATUS lines with a regex; control-center relied on the agent remembering to comment. Both lost results.
learn: lc-wms jobs.py, control-center assistant_reply.py, Paperclip run dispositions (research 12)
rec_reason: A typed verb is checkable, the run manager can write it to the ticket itself, and a missing report is visible instead of silent.

options.label: A structured outcome: hl run report
options.desc: Every run ends by calling hl run report (done, review, blocked or needs-input, summary, next). The run manager writes it to the ticket; no report shows as no outcome.

options.label: The agent comments itself
options.desc: Rely on the agent calling ticket comment and ticket move.

options.label: Parse a STATUS line
options.desc: Scan the final text for a STATUS line, as lc-wms did.

title: Agent sessions
ask: When a role works on a ticket again, does it continue its earlier session?
rec_reason: Resuming keeps context and saves tokens; resetting when the folder or instructions change avoids stale state, as Paperclip does.

options.label: One session per role per ticket
options.desc: Resumed on the next hand-off; reset when the folder or the role's instructions change; a Reset button on the ticket.

options.label: Fresh every run
options.desc: Each run starts clean with the full brief.

options.label: One session per ticket for all roles
options.desc: Every role continues the same conversation.

why: Resuming saves tokens and keeps context, but a stale session can carry wrong assumptions.

title: Isolation for build runs
ask: Where does a build run edit code?
rec_reason: A worktree per ticket keeps parallel builds apart and gives a clean diff to review and merge; analysis roles do not need it.

options.label: A git worktree per ticket for builds
options.desc: Builder and fixer work in a worktree on branch hl/<ticket>; the run shows a diff stat and a Merge button. Other roles work in place.

options.label: In the project folder (today)
options.desc: Runs edit the checked-out project directly.

why: Two builds in one folder overwrite each other, and an unreviewed edit lands straight in the project.

title: Which engine and model a role uses
ask: How is the engine and model for a run chosen?
learn: Paperclip adapterType per agent, control-center backends as data (research 12)
rec_reason: A default per role means no choice in the common case, and an override per hand-off covers the rest.

options.label: Default per role, override per hand-off
options.desc: Settings > Crew sets each role's engine and model; the Next step chip overrides one hand-off.

options.label: Pick on every run
options.desc: Choose engine and model each time.

options.label: One default for all roles
options.desc: Every role uses the workspace default engine.

why: Picking an engine and model on every run is the drop-down problem again; one default for all wastes strong models on simple roles.
